source: Gyurme Dorje 2001, marriage printed pages194–201; White Beryl ff228b–236b

source_notes.paraphrase: Three marriage-divination methods: trigrams for compatibility, numeric squares for travel/departure timing, year signs for ritual procedures.
Five named destiny-element relationship types are used in partner evaluation, with multiple possible narrated outcomes.
Animal-year combinations are presented in distinct lists for compatible affection, many children, prosperity and poor family continuity.
Pre-existing sexagenary-year omen classifications are reused when assessing marriage; this is not a new independent set of predictors.
The text lists six distinct unfavorable animal-year unions: Mouse/Hare, Ox/Tiger, Dragon/Snake, Pig/Dog, Horse/Bird, Monkey/Sheep.
Moonbeams describes a thirteen-pebble compatibility procedure combining four elemental personal forces, calendar inputs, constitutional types and symbolic conjunctions.
Four relationship domains are assigned respectively to vitality, body, destiny and luck comparisons: endurance, family/health, resources and social standing.
The five elemental destiny categories generate fifteen unordered partner combinations with differing claimed children-number and prosperity outcomes.
Collective pebbles use Wood=1, Earth=2, Water=3, Fire=4, Iron=5; an even tally is interpreted as favorable and odd as unfavorable.
Natal months, days and hours are examined for enemy relations, tomb signs and seventh-removed aspects.
The heavenly-medicine chart lists Li/Kham, Khon/Khen, Dva/Gin, Zin/Zon as favorable pair categories.

Direct page-image review confirms the published prose and Plate17 fig4 table list 'Kham/Zin' as the fourth sustaining-vitality pair, while the first pair is 'Li/Zin', duplicating Zin and leaving Zon absent. The same page also lists Kham/Zin in a different favorable grouping. This is an unresolved published-source convention or error; do not silently substitute Zon.

source_issues: CONFIRMED VISIBLE PAIR DUPLICATION: PDF201 / printed200, sustaining-vitality row lists Li/Zin, Khon/Gin, Dva/Khen, Kham/Zin; the printed table itself repeats Zin; original Tibetan and alternative edition unresolved.
